name: Covetousness and the Love of Money

counsel.text: Sin aims always at the utmost; every time it rises up to tempt or entice, might it have its own course, it would go out to the utmost sin in that kind. Every unclean thought or glance would be adultery if it could; every covetous desire would be oppression, every thought of unbelief would be atheism, might it grow to its head.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 2

counsel.text: Water is useful for the sailing of the ship: all the danger is when the water gets into the ship; so the fear is, when the world gets into the heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: It is a sin that wears a cloak, it cloaks itself under the name of frugality and good husbandry. It has many pleas and excuses for itself; more than any other sin: as providing for one's family. The more subtle the sin is, the less discernible it is.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: The root of covetousness is distrust of God's providence. Faith believes that God will provide; that he who feeds the birds will feed his children; that he who clothes the lilies will clothe his lambs; and thus faith overcomes the world. Faith is the cure of care. It not only purifies the heart, but satisfies it; it makes God our portion, and in him we have enough.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: The fourth remedy is to pray for a heavenly mind. Lord, let the loadstone of thy Spirit draw my heart upward. Lord, dig the earth out of my heart; teach me how to possess the world, and not love it; how to hold it in my hand, and not let it get into my heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: Where one thousand are destroyed by the world's frowns, ten thousand are destroyed by the world's smiles. The world, siren-like, it sings us and sinks us; it kisses us, and betrays us, like Judas; it kisses us and smites us under the fifth rib, like Joab.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: Tell me, you that say all things under the sun are vanity, if you do really believe what you say, why do you spend more thoughts and time on the world, than you do on Christ, heaven, and your immortal souls? Why do you then neglect your duty towards God, to get the world? Why do you then so eagerly pursue after the world, and are so cold in your pursuing after God, Christ, and holiness?
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: Covetousness, when men will be richer than God would have them, troubles all; it troubles the house, the whole family, and the house within us, our precious soul, which should be a quiet house for God's spirit to dwell in, whose seat is a quiet spirit. If men would follow Christ's method, and 'seek first the kingdom of heaven,' Mat. 6. 33, all other things would be cast upon them.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 25

counsel.text: 'Oh!' saith Satan, 'if thou wouldst but venture on a lie—make bold a little with God in such a command—this wedge of gold is thine, and that advantage will accrue to thy estate.' Now faith will teach the soul to reply, 'I am well provided for already, Satan; I need not thy pension; why should I play the thief for that which, if good, God hath promised to give?'
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Thus, some are slaves to their estates; it is said, 'Their heart goes after their covetousness'—that is, as the servant after the master, who dares not be from his back. Their money is the master, and hath the best keeping. Their heart waits on it, shall I say as a servant after his master? yea, as a dog at his master's foot.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.opening: Faithful Father, the earth is yours and everything in it, and you are the treasure of my heart; I bless you that you have promised never to leave or forsake your children, and that I may come to you through Jesus Christ.
prayers.text: I confess that I have coveted. I have wanted more than you have given me, and I have set my heart on things that will rust and pass away. I have looked to money for a security that belongs to you alone, and I have measured my life by what I own. My covetousness is idolatry: it has put a created thing in the place of the Creator. I have tried to serve two masters, and I have been tight-fisted toward you and toward my neighbor. I do not want only to escape its worry and debt; I want to hate it because it robs you of the trust that is yours. Forgive me, Lord. Christ, though he was rich, became poor for my sake, so that I might become rich in him. He is my treasure, and in him I have an inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade. For his sake pardon me. Holy Spirit, put this greed to death, and make me content and open-handed.
prayers.closing: I thank you that you did not spare your own Son, and that with him you will graciously give me all things. To you be the glory, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, my portion for ever. Amen.

prayers.title: When I want more
prayers.opening: O Lord, you are my portion and my inheritance, and in your presence there is fullness of joy.
prayers.text: Lord, my heart is pulled toward something I do not have. Stop me here, before I buy it, scheme for it, or brood over it. You are my portion, and you know what I need before I ask. Life does not consist in the abundance of possessions; I brought nothing into this world and I can take nothing out. Turn my eyes back to what you have already given, and let me thank you for it now. Lord Jesus, you had nowhere to lay your head, and you were rich toward God. Be my treasure. Holy Spirit, loosen my grip, and make me glad to give something away today.
prayers.closing: Blessed be your name, for you give me all things richly to enjoy. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: For a generous heart
prayers.opening: Most generous Father, you love a cheerful giver, for you are the greatest Giver of all, and you gave me your own beloved Son.
prayers.text: Make me like you. Teach me to hold money and things as your steward and not their owner, and to use them for your glory and my neighbor's good. Make me honest in my work, faithful and joyful in my giving, and free from the love of money. Let me be rich in good works and ready to share. Fix my hope not on uncertain riches but on you, who richly provide everything for me to enjoy. And as I let go of what I cannot keep, let me lay hold of the life that is truly life.
prayers.closing: Thanks be to you for your inexpressible gift, through Jesus Christ my Lord. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing covetousness and love of the world
prayers.opening: Whom have we in heaven but thee; and there is none upon earth that we desire besides thee, or in comparison of thee: when our flesh and our heart fail, be thou the strength of our heart, and our portion for ever; the portion of our inheritance in the other world, and of our cup in this, and then we will say that the lines are fallen to us in pleasant places, and that we have a goodly heritage.
prayers.text: Our conversation has not been without covetousness, nor have we learned in every state to be content with such things as we have. Who can say he is clean from that love of money, which is the root of all evil, that covetousness which is idolatry? We have sought great things to ourselves, when thou hast said, Seek them not.
prayers.closing: Now to God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father, be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 2 and 7

prayers.title: That the love of the world be rooted out
prayers.opening: Thou art the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness or shadow of turning, and from whom proceedeth every good and perfect gift.
prayers.text: Let the love of the world be rooted out of us, and that covetousness which is idolatry; and let the love of God in Christ be rooted in us. Shed abroad that love in our hearts by the Holy Ghost, and give us to love thee the Lord our God with all our heart, and soul, and mind, and might; and to do all we do in religion from a principle of love to thee.
prayers.closing: Do for us exceeding abundantly above what we are able to ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us: And supply all our needs according to thy riches in glory by Christ Jesus. To God, only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 9 and 7

examinationQuestions: What did you want today that you did not have, and what did you think having it would give you that God has not already given you in Christ?
Where have you looked to money or possessions for the safety, comfort, or worth that only God can give?
Where has covetousness dressed itself up as wisdom, thrift, or providing for those you love?
Have work, buying, or planning how to get more crowded out prayer, the Word, or the Lord's Day this week?
When did you last give freely to your church or to someone in need, and did you give gladly?
If God took away what you own tomorrow, would Christ still be enough for you? Ask God to make it so.
fleeActions: Close the shopping page or app and put your phone down. Do not buy anything today that you had not planned to buy this morning.
Write down three things God has given you this week, and thank him for each one out loud.
Give something away today, quietly: money to your church's deacons, or help to someone in need.
Open your Bible to Matthew 6:19-34 and read it slowly. Then pray it back to God in your own words.
Message a brother or sister in your church and tell them honestly that you are fighting greed. Ask them to pray for you today.
Go and do the next task of your calling with your whole heart, as work for the Lord and not for gain.

afterFallReadings.text: God can bestow a jewel upon us, but we fall so in love with it, that we forget Him that gave it.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 10

afterFallReadings.text: Yea, let me add, that never any soul did or shall perish by the power of any lust, sin, or corruption, who could raise his soul by faith to an expectation of relief from Jesus Christ.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
